---
title: "Manual Page"
format: html
---

Each Quarto Manual page is one operational step in the manual. A page should
tell the user:

- what must already be true;
- what they need to do now;
- how they can prove the step worked.

To make that structure explicit, every page must use three semantic block
types:

- exactly one `.manual-prereq` block;
- one or more `.manual-procedure` blocks;
- exactly one `.manual-check` block.

These blocks give the page a predictable structure for both the reader and the
manual tooling. They also let the manual derive a checklist view across all
pages without turning the manual into a hidden workflow engine.

## Required Page Structure

Start each page with normal Quarto metadata:

```yaml
---
title: "Assemble Python Environment"
manual:
  page: 2
---
```

Then write the page using the required manual blocks.

### 1. Prerequisite Block

The prerequisite block explains what the user must already have before this
step is actionable. This is the place to inspect the current project state,
load shared helper code, or confirm that earlier manual steps are complete.

There must be exactly one prerequisite block on the page. In this manual,
the prerequisite block should include the shared checklist definition so that
each page starts from the same declared manual state.[^1]

[^1]: Notebook authoring can make cross-page state hard to reason about.
By keeping the checklist definition in one included file, each page can
recreate the same shared base objects in its own execution context. This
gives authors one source of truth while avoiding hidden dependence on
state from another page.

::: {.manual-prereq}

## Prerequisite Block Example

<!-- For computations during rendering, the following will run the class definition -->

{{< include impl_python.qmd >}}


This page assumes the project directory exists and that the user has already
chosen an environment name.

```{python}
from pathlib import Path

assert project, "Expected project to be defined. Did you include the checklist.qmd file and run the first page?"
assert project.project_root.is_dir(), "Expected project root to be a directory"

environment_dir = project.project_root / ".venv"
```

:::


### 2. Procedure Blocks

Procedure blocks contain the actual work of the page. A page may need one
procedure block or several, depending on how much scaffolding you want to give
the user.

There must be at least one procedure block on the page.

```markdown
::: {.manual-procedure}
Create the Python virtual environment.

```{python}
import venv

venv.create(environment_dir, with_pip=True)
```
:::
```

You can use multiple procedure blocks when the step has distinct parts, such as
writing a file and then installing dependencies.

### 3. Check Block

The check block proves whether the page succeeded. This should inspect the real
project state and fail clearly when the step is incomplete or incorrect.

There must be exactly one check block on the page.

```markdown
::: {.manual-check}
Confirm that the environment directory was created.

```{python}
assert environment_dir.exists(), "Expected .venv to exist"
assert environment_dir.is_dir(), "Expected .venv to be a directory"
```
:::
```

## Complete Example

The following page uses the required manual structure from beginning to end.

```markdown
---
title: "Assemble Python Environment"
manual:
  page: 2
---

This page creates the project's Python environment.

::: {.manual-prereq}
Before continuing, confirm that you are in the project root and that Python is
available.

```{python}
from pathlib import Path

project_root = Path(".")
environment_dir = project_root / ".venv"
```
:::

Some projects may also explain why this environment is needed and how it will
be used by later pages.

::: {.manual-procedure}
Create the virtual environment.

```{python}
import venv

venv.create(environment_dir, with_pip=True)
```
:::

::: {.manual-procedure}
Record the activation command for the user.

```{python}
activation_hint = "source .venv/bin/activate"
print(activation_hint)
```
:::

::: {.manual-check}
Verify that the environment now exists.

```{python}
assert environment_dir.exists(), "Expected .venv to exist"
assert environment_dir.is_dir(), "Expected .venv to be a directory"
```
:::
```

## Authoring Rules

When writing a page, keep these rules in mind:

- use exactly one `.manual-prereq` block;
- use at least one `.manual-procedure` block;
- use exactly one `.manual-check` block;
- let checks inspect real files, paths, configs, logs, or rendered outputs when
  possible;
- keep the page focused on one operational step.

The goal of a page is not just to explain a step. The goal is to help the user
perform that step and prove that it is complete.
